title_original: European Film Academy unveils shortlist for 2027 European Film Awards
excerpt_original: Shortlist includes major festival winners such as Fjord, Woman Unknown, Yellow Letters, Tender Loving Care and La Bola Negra.

blocks.text: Source: Tudor Panduru
‘Fjord’
The European Film Academy has shortlisted 68 feature-length films for a possible nomination for the European Film Awards, which take place on January 16 in Athens.
The shortlist comprises 45 feature films, 15 documentary films and eight animated feature films from 40 countries. 25 film of the films are directed or co-directed by women.
Scroll down for full shortlist

The feature film shortlist includes high-profile festival titles such as Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner Fjord , Venice Golden Lion winner Woman Unknown by May el-Toukhy, Berlinale Golden Bear winner Yellow Letters by İlker Çatak and Toronto audience prize winner La Bola Negra by Javier Calvo & Javier Ambrossi.

Other festival victors shortlisted include San Sebastian Golden Shell winner Tender Loving Care by Mike Leigh, Florin Şerban’s Locarno Golden Leopard winner You Don’t Belong Here and Sundance world dramatic cinema winner Shame And Money by Visar Morina.

Elsewhere, the shortlist brings together an array of festival favourites, spanning Fatherland by Pawel Pawlikowski, which shared the Cannes best director prize with La Bola Negra, and Simon Stone’s Elsinore which just opened the BFI London Film Festival.

From Cannes, Pedro Almodóvar’s Bitter Christmas is on the shortlist, as is Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Minotaur, Lukas Dhont’s Coward and Antonin Baudry’s two-part De Gaulle biopic. Venice titles include Florian Zeller’s Bunker and Werner Herzog’s Bucking Fastard.

The documentary shortlist spans Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor’s NAZA , winner of the jury prize at Venice through to Pegah Ahangarani’s Rehearsals For A Revolution , winner of the Cannes documentary award and Biljana Tutorov & Petar Glomazić ’s To Hold A Mountain, winner of the Sundance international documentary prize.
The animation shortlist includes Annecy audience and jury prize winner Iron Boy by Louis Clichy and Cannes premiere Jim Queen by Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané.

The shortlisted feature and documentary films have been chosen by members of the European Film Academy board and invited European experts, while the shortlisted animated feature films were chosen by a selection committee composed of members of the Academy Board and invited experts in cooperation with Cartoon, the European Association of Animation Film.

The shortlist announcement is the first step in EFA’s awarding procedure. In the coming weeks, the 5,700 members of the European Film Academy will watch the shortlisted films and vote for the nominations, except for the European discovery – Prix Fipresci, European short film, European young audience award, LUX audience award and honorary awards, which have separate selection procedures

The nominations for key categories will be announced on November 14 during the Thessaloniki International Film Festival, while the European young audience award nominations will be announced on November 1 at the International Film Festival Glasgow. The short film nominations will be revealed at the Seville European Film Festival on November 13 The nominees for the LUX audience award will be unveiled on 25 November.
